# n² + n + 41 is prime for every natural number n

**ID**: `cpt-nt-conj-euler-all-prime`

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

## Statement

For every natural number n (0 included), f(n) = n² + n + 41 is a prime number.

This is the pattern an exploration of n = 0, …, 39 suggests; it is **false** (see Evidence and Status). Plan: `cpt-nt-rplan-euler-polynomial`.

## Formal Statement

```lean
Euler.conj_euler_all_prime : ∀ (n : Nat), Euler.isPrime (Euler.f n) = true
```

- **Stub**: `examples/euler-polynomial/lean-euler/Stubs.lean`, `lake env lean Stubs.lean` in `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0`, 2026-10-13
- **Concordance**: `Nat` → "Natural number"; `Euler.f` → "Euler's polynomial"; `Euler.isPrime … = true` → "p is prime"

## Origin

Pattern in exploration: `examples/euler-polynomial/enumerate.py` (EXPLORE phase, 2026-10-13), line `f(n) prime for every n < 40: True` — the first forty values are all prime, extrapolated to every n (the historically famous trap).

## Evidence

| Region checked | Method | Record | Result |
|----------------|--------|--------|--------|
| n < 100 | exact (trial division) | `examples/euler-polynomial/enumerate.py`, line `n < 100 with f(n) composite: [40, 41, 44, …]` | counterexample: n = 40, f(40) = 1681 = 41² (and 13 more composite values below 100) |

The instance check refuted the statement before any attempt (P4). The counterexample is one closed term, so instead of a CLAIM + CERTIFICATE it was formalized directly as a tier-C refutation (Attempts; recorded as a deviation there).
